newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hoechst unit set to list shares in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst unit set to list shares in 1997.

text.p: German drugs and chemicals group Hoechst AG diagnostics division Behring Diagnostics plans to enter a joint-venture with U.S. group Dade International and list shares on the New York bourse this year.
"We plan to list the shares very quickly, still in this calendar year," Uwe Bicker, the head of Behring Diagnostics told Reuters in a telephone interview.
The bourse listing would likely occur in two tranches, with securities houses Goldman Sachs and Bain Capital paring their stakes, Bicker said.
He added that the listing would likely be scheduled for the second half of this year.

Hoechst will hold a 32 percent minority stake in the new group, Dade Behring International, and have an option to acquire a larger stake. Bicker said the joint-venture would turn the group into one of the world's biggest diagnostics businesses, active in producing equipment for therapeutic drug monitoring and plasma protein monitoring.
"These two groups are very complementary and there is virtually no overlap," Bicker said, adding that Behring was strong in Europe, while Dade was strong in the U.S.

Bicker also said the joint-venture, still awaiting approval from cartel authorities, was necessary to offer Behring the necessary "muscle in the U.S.", which had not been completely achieved with the takeover of Syva.

A key result will be that the new group will soon be able to raise its return on sales, Bicker said forecasting a return of 12 percent in the next several years. Last year, Behring posted a return of nine percent.
Bicker was unable to say what the restructuring costs might be or offer an outlook for 1997 profits.
Behring swung to an 88 million mark profit last year from an eight million mark loss, incurred largely through restructuring costs associated with the acquisition of U.S. group Syva.
